💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov.
  • XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Recent findings suggest that three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to glitch loans and track repayments onchain.".

Sources indicate that the model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool indicated the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

In a recent development, through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

Sources indicate that the amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

6 Best Heart Rate Monitors, Tested by Our Fitness Editors

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that TRAINING WITHOUT TRACKING is like shooting a basketball without knowing where the hoop is, especially if you have an ultimate goal like running a marathon or increasing your VO2 max.
  • A few of the most important insights are heart rate variability (HRV), which describes the difference in time between the beats of your heart, and resting heart rate (RHR), which is the number of times your heart pumps while you are awake, relaxed and not moving.
  • Understanding your HRV can help you make better workout choices and understand when it's time to recover.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that TRAINING WITHOUT TRACKING is like shooting a basketball without knowing where the hoop is, especially if you have an ultimate goal like running a marathon or increasing your VO2 max. Many people reach a point in their fitness journey where they hit a plateau, and more often than not, that flatline results from not having the right information. So if you're hitting the gym on a regular basis and putting in the work, it can be important to make sure that you are getting all the relevant health insights to make sure you're using your time efficiently.

A few of the most important insights are heart rate variability (HRV), which describes the difference in time between the beats of your heart, and resting heart rate (RHR), which is the number of times your heart pumps while you are awake, relaxed and not moving. Heart rate monitors (HRMs) are the best way to get this data.

Understanding your HRV can help you make better workout choices and understand when it's time to recover. Generally speaking, your resting heart rate will become lower as your fitness level increases, indicating more efficient heart function and improved cardiovascular fitness. “Over time (and months of tracking your resting heart rate), you'll notice patterns. Maybe your RHR spikes every weekend, in part because you're out late Saturday nights. Or it's lower on Mondays, because you go to bed earlier on Sundays," states MH Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. "All of this data can help you make smart lifestyle tweaks that aid your overall wellness — and set you up to move, look, and feel your best and most alert, whether you're in the gym or at the office.”.

With the holidays coming up fast, it’s a good time to add a heart rate monitor to your wish list. It can help you start your Fresh Year’s training goals on a data-driven note, and allow you to track your progress over time.

Ready to take your training to the next level? Read on to find the best heart rate monitors for you and what to consider when looking for a HRM.

We've been raving about Whoop for years, and it's still one of our favorite fitness trackers simply because it collects so much useful data. This stylish and understated device uses PPG sensors to continuously check your heart rate, and can use the data it captures to figure out when your deepest sleep is happening.

Recent findings suggest that every day it delivers a recovery percentage and suggests the level of activity you should aim for, whether that a five-mile run or a rest day. In the past, the brand stuck with a simple black band, but these days there are more color and style options for anyone wanting to elevate the look of their HRM.

I personally am a fan of the ability to check my insights when I want, without a distractingly bright screen that pulls my attention.

It has been revealed that while products like the Whoop band and the Oura Ring are relatively upcoming on the scene, Garmin has been making wearable fitness trackers for a long time now. This heart rate monitor transmits real-time heart rate data over ANT+ connectivity and Bluetooth, giving you the immediate feedback you need to take your performance to the next level.

This Garmin comes with a rechargeable battery with a seriously long life (two months). It charges easily using the provided 4-pin charging cable, similar to the ones that come with their watches.

We were also impressed with how comfortable this strap is to wear, made out of a lightweight nylon weave. For placement, you want to put the sensor in the middle of your ribcage against your skin, not over your clothes, so that it can get the best readings. Once you are done with your run, you will be able to connect it to your smartphone or Garmin watch via Bluetooth, and then pull up your stats from the menu option.

It has been revealed that because this Garmin has Bluetooth, it is also able to connect pretty simply to cardio machines at your gym like treadmills if you want to track your workouts there. If you are a Garmin fan, and want even more functionality and access to the Garmin Connect app, you may want to spring for the Garmin HRM Pro model (about $60 more).

Read More: Best Fitness Trackers, Tested by Us.

Recent findings suggest that this is a subtle and sleek way to monitor your heart rate throughout the day. Most people aren't going to wear a ring like this while lifting weights, which is why we love the Oura Ring to track those notable metrics during the 23 hours of the day that you're not at the gym. What's most impressive about the Oura Ring is its small size, and how one small ring can monitor your sleep, steps, and heart rate.

Sources indicate that this ring gives you all the information you need to make improvements in your daily health and well-being. For those looking to try a smart ring for the first time, it doesn't get better than Oura, which is why it took the top spot in our best smart rings testing and this head-to-head piece against the Samsung Galaxy Ring.

It has been revealed that read More: The Oura Ring Vs. the Galaxy Ring.

It has been revealed that the Apple Watch is by far one of the most popular smartwatches on the market, and like the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, it also tracks quite a lot of data, including heart rate. Although not as accurate as the chest bands, the Apple Watch 12 gets the job done well enough for the casual fitness goer.

It has been revealed that in addition to heart rate, it also features an SpO2 sensor to monitor blood oxygen level readings, an ECG to test for atrial fibrillation, fitness tracking, sleep monitoring, and all the run-of-the-mill smartwatch features. Our editors have already spent some time with this latest release, and it's fair to say we're suitably impressed.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 is essentially a wearable personal trainer and advisor powered by AI. With built-in pace coaching and a heart rate monitor, you can add and customize your workouts for maximum efficiency, helping you reach your fitness goals in no time. It connects to your smartphone so you can easily take calls, receive texts, or pull up directions with the flick of your wrist.

The newer design is certainly better looking than previous editions. The integrated Run Coach also impressed some of our editors, guiding those who require additional motivation.

That being mentioned, despite the fact that the Galaxy Watch 8 supports iOS and iPhone users through its companion app, those users might be better over going for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for the additional integrations. The heart rate measurements and sleep tracking is where this device really shines, which is perfect for those looking for a upcoming HRM.

Read more: Best Smartwatches, Tested By Us.

According to recent reports, while it’s not the latest version, the Pixel Watch 4 from Google is packed with useful features beginners will appreciate. (The Pixel Watch 5 is the newest iteration, but significantly more expensive.) One of our favorites is Active Zone Minutes, which uses your resting heart rate to gauge exercise effort and give you a buzz when it's time to step up the intensity so you can make the most of your workouts. It monitors activity, sleep, and nightly blood oxygen levels, tracking your trends over time to see notable changes in your overall health.

According to recent reports, this is a great pick for anyone looking to get great health insights from a wrist piece, who also would like a subtly stylish look. Since Google now owns Fitbit, this watch features some of that great Fitbit technology, which means there are a lot of great integrations if you have a Google account. But because of this, the pairing with iOS devices is not optimal. Something to take into consideration if you're an Apple user.

Google also knows how to make app experiences easy on latest owners, including older users without a lot of time with technology.

The biggest determination you need to make before purchasing is what your primary goal is for the heart rate monitor. Competitive triathletes may want to splurge on a top-shelf device that wraps around your chest for the most accurate data. Whereas beginners or more casual users might opt for a more modest option they can wear throughout the day (like a general fitness tracker) for daily health insights. Perhaps you spend a lot of time on the golf course and want to know how your heart handles hours of walking combined with the stress of trying to make par. Of course, you may be one of those high-performing individuals who uses both.

Recent findings suggest that beyond finding a device that fits your performance needs, you also need one that fits well on your body. This depends on whether you choose a chest strap, a wristband, or a smart ring. In most cases, the sensors need to be secured tightly against your body to get accurate readings. Take accurate body measurements before ordering offline, and be prepared to return for a different size if you need to (especially with something like a chest strap). If you are looking into smart rings, many of the options, like the Oura Ring we list, will ship out sizing kits for a small fee to get the correct fit.

Great data is useless if you don’t have an easy means of getting it. For devices without screens, make sure you check which smartphones and apps they are compatible with. They will usually connect with your personal devices through Bluetooth. For devices with screens, check images of the user interface to make sure you’ll enjoy it. Of course, the devices we are suggesting here with screens will display all the important information you’ll want. But some may have better compatibility with iOS or Android, which you’ll want to consider.

With the exception of the Apple Watches (Ultra 3 and Series 11) and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 (two heart rate monitors that are equal parts smartwatch), the heart rate monitors we tested are all designed to run for days (even weeks) on a single charge. We love a heart rate monitor that needs minimal charging, and we also love one that lasts a long time in non-connected mode. Two heart rate monitors that surprised us when testing battery life include the Garmin HRM-Dual (3.5 years if used for one hour a day) and the Oura Ring (7 days while on).

In a recent development, being the Fitness and Commerce Editor at Men's Health, it's my job to evaluate the latest and greatest training gear. This includes fitness trackers, and throughout the year, I get the latest designs from the best brands, both upcoming and old. I am also a certified trainer, and my personal training includes a wide range of exercises, from boxing to lifting to sprint work. But this story was a collective effort by several editors, who were enlisted to try different models and types of trackers based on their preferences.

We tested each tracker for at least two weeks and put it through a range of exercise scenarios, from treadmill sprints to weighted pull-ups to deadlifts. My fellow testers included certified trainers who also happen to be editors at Men's Health, like Samuel. For devices that have been around for several updates, we've used most of them since they hit the market. Our tested selection didn't focus on chasing trends. Instead, our picks of the best fitness trackers provide great value and performance at reasonable price points for the data they provide.

All of these factors went into finding our favorite heart rate monitors.

According to recent reports, charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. Following an early life in athletics, Charles became a NASM-certified trainer and began writing programs alongside the most respected coaches in the world. Hästens 2000T Mattress, Tested and Reviewed (2026)

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that from the moment I touched down in Sweden, the focus was on sleep.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Swedish manufacturer, which has been making beds since 1852, sits atop the luxury market for mattresses.
  • According to recent reports, but what earns a mattress luxury status?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that from the moment I touched down in Sweden, the focus was on sleep. Coming off a red-eye flight from New York with only two hours of rest (three if we’re being generous), there was nothing more I wanted to do than lie down. Luckily, a Hästens mattress—the reason for my trip—awaited me at the hotel and soon provided what was perhaps the most luxurious nap I’d ever experienced.

Recent findings suggest that the Swedish manufacturer, which has been making beds since 1852, sits atop the luxury market for mattresses. The brand—whose name is Swedish for “the horse’s”—has a consuming commitment to craftsmanship, and its horsehair-filled beds are handmade. That level of focus also comes with a hefty price tag, which is why the brand is perhaps best known by the general public for its presence in celebrity homes (or possibly its cameo in an Emily in Paris episode as the subject of the titular character’s latest marketing campaign). But reputation aside, Hästens knows how to make a damn good bed.

According to recent reports, but what earns a mattress luxury status? And what is it actually like to sleep on one from Hästens? After touring the brand’s main factory in Köping, Sweden, I’ve laid my head on one of its most popular mattresses, the 2000T, for the last few months, all in the name of trying to understand how much money a good night’s sleep is worth.

Price listed is for a queen size bed.

To the average person, horsehair is likely not the first mattress fill material that comes to mind—if it comes to mind at all. Gel, innerspring, memory foam, cotton, or some combination of those are way more common. But horsehair has a historic precedent, having been used in beds for many periods of human history, particularly when horses were the primary mode of transportation.

Much of the present-day reason for using the material comes from a scientific point of view: Horsehair strands are naturally hollow, which Hästens claims “transports any excess heat and moisture from your body during deep sleep.” Additionally, when cut and treated, the strands form a helix shape, which works in conjunction with the metal springs in a bed for a strong base of support.

Exterior of the Hastens factory in Köping, Sweden, designed by British architect Ralph Erskine.

Recent findings suggest that an hour and a half train ride northwest from Stockholm, the small town of Köping is so quiet, you might expect to see a horse roaming the streets—maybe having recently received a haircut to donate to the mattress cause. When thinking of the word factory, one may expect a loud, gigantic warehouse filled with whirring machines and assembly lines moving so quickly you can hardly see the product before it whizzes past. But the Hästens factory possessed a quite different vibe. Sure, there is still machinery and expansive production areas, but it was fairly quiet, and I felt that the energy was more akin to a pottery studio than an industrial plant: craft-forward, methodical, and with a focus on handmade artistry. In fact, my host told me that only around 100 people work in the main factory, most of whom are from the area, highlighting the manufacturer as a point of pride for the local community.

In a recent development, walking into the processing room of the factory, I was greeted by a small mountain of horsehair on the floor. It looked much more like a soft version of steel wool than the shiny mane and tail I was envisioning. That’s because the hair is cut down to small strands prior to being integrated into the mattresses. The hair also goes through several disinfecting and processing treatments before it even arrives at the factory. Taking a clump between my hands, I was surprised by its springiness. (And horse girls need not fear about animal welfare: My host for the trip confirmed that their suppliers from farms around the world aren’t killing horses for their hair, the mane and tail cuttings they receive are ethically sourced.).

The blue check pattern, developed by fourth-generation company leader Jack Ryde in 1978, is synonymous with the brand. So much so that a check-laden Mercedes was waiting to drive us from the train station to the factory.

Each layer of horsehair in the mattress is fluffed by hand and placed between sheets of cotton and wool.

Every aspect of the bed creation process happens by hand: prepping the layers of wool and horsehair for the filling, arranging and securing steel springs, framing the Swedish pine base. I watched workers build each part of the bed with a devoted level of care. The only fully automated aspect of the bed manufacturing that I witnessed on my tour was stitching a pattern onto the top mattress to give it a signature tufted texture. But even that is hand-sewn on certain bed models.

Industry observers note that quality is tested at every step, and if something isn’t up to par, production restarts. For some models, including the Grand Vividus (at the top of Hästens range), there are only a select few craftspeople who are trained in the production process. Much of the brand’s higher price tag comes down to that heightened level of labor and care. If someone on the team is sick or is simply just working slower on a given day, the production timeline increases to accommodate the quality level that Hästens demands: perfection.

My loaned mattress also included a full set of Hästens bedding.

The 2000T is one of the brand’s best sellers, falling around the middle of their price range.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to my sleep setup, my mattress was the element that I’d been putting off upgrading for years. I only leveled up my years-old box spring with a mattress topper a few years ago. I tend to prioritize bedding when buying latest duds for the bedroom, and because I’m consistently testing various sets of sheets for AD, my focus tends to be on how linens can visually transform a space rather than shift my physical experience. All to say, upgrading to a Hästens was like going from a hand-me-down sedan to a Lamborghini.

In a recent development, before receiving the loaned mattress for testing, I tried out different models in person at the Manhattan flagship store in NoMad, an experience Hästens coins the Sleep Spa. As a staff member talked me through proper spinal alignment and notable pressure points, I lay on various models in a Goldilocks-esque journey to see which mattress was the right fit. True to Hästens’ superlative level of service, even this part of the process felt curated. Ambient music played, lights dimmed, and I was given two pillows and a duvet for snuggling. The meditative process made me focus on how my body responded to each mattress. As a combination stomach-and-side sleeper—and someone who likes to sit on her bed—I selected the 2000T (in firm) after around an hour of sampling.

Despite being a firmer model, the 2000T still contours to my body in a way that I can only describe as cushy. The horsehair filling provides a unique springiness that the compression of memory foam or cotton can’t quite replicate. It sinks in just enough to give my shoulders enough space when I sleep on my side, but is supportive enough to keep my hips from dropping out of alignment for the nights I’m on my stomach.

In a recent development, as I mentioned, I often lounge on bed to read, play video games, or what have you. While facilitating sleep is the primary function of a mattress, I was keen to see how its edge control and support would stand up to this alternative usage. I was surprised by how little back pain I sustained after reading sessions that extended beyond two hours. Because of its reinforced springs at the corners and edges, I could also sit right on the edge of the mattress without feeling like I was going to roll off.

The aspect of the horsehair fill I was most intrigued to test was its claim of moisture and heat-wicking properties. I like to be fully swaddled underneath my duvet, top sheet, and sometimes even another blanket when I sleep, which can be a recipe for waking up sweaty. That hasn’t happened once with the 2000T. The foam topper on my prior bed often trapped heat, and I’d wake up in the middle of the night to rip off some of the layers of bedding in order to cool down. With the Hästens, though, I can be as greedy with my bedding as I want to be without overheating.

The ‘massage’ portion lasted about 10 minutes.

As part of their high bar of customer service, the company offers a free recalibration program from select stores to help maintain the longevity of the mattress and mitigate any compression issues. The product care program involves Hästens staffers visiting your home (typically once a year) to flip and massage the mattress—the latter consisting of a person marching back and forth across the mattress to redistribute the fill materials. I can safely say having a grown man in booties walk in circles on top of my bed for 10 minutes was one of the oddest moments of my life, but sleeping on the bed that night, I could feel the difference. While there weren’t any severe lumps formed in my two-month testing period, the process smoothed out any compression in the areas I most often lay.

Although I’ve only slept on the 2000T for around two months, I can see a noticeable change in how my body feels after a night’s rest. I struggle with hypermobility and have a family history of arthritis, so I’m on high alert about how my joints feel upon waking up in the morning. On my old bed, I typically awoke with some pain in my hips and a stiff lower back. While sleeping on the Hästens hasn’t fully eliminated any achiness, I essentially ceased needing to do the typical stretching routine I used to perform in the morning in order to get my body ready for the day.

Down pillows were provided by the brand for my loaner bed.

The structure of Hästens beds includes a top mattress and middle mattress, the former mimicking a thick topper.

According to recent reports, as someone who has notoriously bad nighttime habits (like plentiful screen time), I had accepted I’d only be able to expect a low level of restfulness from my sleep. I was content with a solid six hours and low-level of back achiness in the morning, thinking I couldn’t consistently adjust my routine to improve my experience. Sleeping on the Hästens 2000T has changed that mindset drastically. It’s without a doubt the best mattress I’ve ever slept on.

However, it’s easy for me to say this bed is worth it because I didn’t have to pay the steep price tag of $74,780 to try it out in my home. Yes, Hästens exceeded my expectations when it came to sleep, but after the testing period ends, I don’t anticipate a sudden change in my finances that would allow me to invest in my own 2000T. Although the brand’s beds are built to last a lifetime, and we spend a third of our lives asleep, the question of how much a good night’s sleep is really worth is highly individualized.

This experience more broadly made me consider where we are most willing to invest in when it comes to our home spaces. Sure, a covetable mattress like one from Hästens may not be as flashy as other significant-ticket purchases, like a giant flat screen, but I’d posit a splurge has few better use cases than on something you return to each night.

Lucid (LCID) indicates service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.

Recent findings suggest that the automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.

Recent findings suggest that lucid confirmed the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings. Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.

In a recent development, the hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a big hiring push for a manufacturer that laid off 18% of its workforce in June, its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.

It has been revealed that and owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.

Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, remarked the company is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”.

Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:.

Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.

Industry observers note that outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first company-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.

Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.

A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-concern. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.

In a recent development, it’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.

Sources indicate that for context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.

This is the right move, and it’s overdue.

According to recent reports, lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if we found its software wasn’t ready. But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.

Recent findings suggest that so growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a substantial deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.

The problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.

Industry observers note that on the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

Both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these new plans.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”.

In a recent development, the registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

However, an key distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

It has been revealed that consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being rolled out in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

Recent findings suggest that these numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

This, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I test a lot of electric bikes, which means I also spend a lot of time wearing bicycle helmets. And while most helmets tend to fall into the decidedly unexciting category of “necessary safety equipment,” UNIT 1 has managed to make a couple that I actually get excited about wearing.

I’ve been using both the UNIT 1 FARO and the new NEON, and despite taking fairly different approaches, they’ve both become regular go-to helmets for me.

The FARO is the more futuristic-looking of the two, and it’s also the one that really leans into the “smart helmet” concept.

The helmet includes MIPS protection to reduce rotational impact during a collision, as well as integrated lighting on both the front and rear, including a large customizable rear lighting area made up of dozens of LEDs.

That large rear LED array is a feature I particularly appreciate since visibility is such a major part of cycling safety.

According to recent reports, A helmet obviously can’t force drivers to pay attention, but I’d rather give them as many opportunities as possible to see me. The hidden light area below the obvious LED light bar adds a lot of extra visibility.

You can see just how vivid it is in the GIF below, though in real life it looks even better!

The FARO’s lighting system works with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote, which adds turn signals controlled right from the bars.

The system can also provide automatic brake-light functionality, giving you another way to communicate with traffic around you.

Sources indicate that I’ll admit that turn signals on bicycles can sometimes feel a bit gimmicky, especially when they’re so close together that drivers can’t really tell which direction is flashing. But putting them high up on the helmet makes them considerably more visible, and the little wireless handlebar remote makes operating them incredibly easy.

Industry observers note that the rechargeable lighting is also convenient. I’ve topped up the helmet from a power bank while out and about, meaning you don’t necessarily need to find a wall outlet if you realize your helmet is running low. The rear LED light bar also turns green and illuminates along the length of the bar to let you know what percentage of charge the battery has reached. The only way it could be clearer would be with a screen, but we’re still talking about a helmet here, not a phone.

There are other smart features packed in too, including crash detection and app-based customization.

The tradeoff is weight. At around 640 grams for a medium, the FARO is noticeably heavier than a conventional bicycle helmet. It doesn’t bother me much once I’m riding, and I’ve found the helmet comfortable, but you definitely know there’s more helmet up there. Each time I pick it up, I’m reminded that it’s not just the basic little foam shell that I’ve been wearing for the last few years.

Then there’s the price. At around $230 (or $195 during the current Black Friday sale period), this isn’t a cheap helmet. You’re paying for all of that technology, lighting, and design.

As much as I like the FARO, I’ve also become a big fan of the UNIT 1 NEON.

In a recent development, at roughly 430 grams in a medium, it’s significantly lighter than the FARO, and that difference is immediately noticeable. It’s also a bit cheaper at around $210 (or $178 during the Black Friday sale period) while still packing several of the smart features that make UNIT 1’s helmets interesting.

You still get MIPS rotational protection, crash detection, integrated rear lighting, app connectivity, and compatibility with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote for turn signals and brake-light functionality.

Industry observers note that I do wish the NEON had a front light like the FARO. That’s probably the biggest feature I miss when switching between the two. But the NEON makes up for it with one of my favorite features on either helmet: its magnetic face shield.

The shield is ridiculously easy to attach and remove. You don’t even need to carefully line it up. I just need to get it somewhere near the mounting points with one hand and the powerful magnets basically grab it out of the air and snap it into position.

That means I can easily add or remove it one-handed, even while riding.

The photochromic shield is clear enough for night riding but darkens when exposed to bright sunlight, giving you sun protection without requiring separate daytime and nighttime shields. I’ve found that incredibly convenient, especially on rides that transition from daylight into evening. I hate that I can’t wear my sunglasses for eye protection at night, and a lens like this solves that issue.

The NEON also gets something particularly important for faster e-bike riders: NTA 8776 certification. That’s the Dutch standard designed specifically around higher-speed e-bike uses at up to 45 km/h (28 mph). For the Class 3 e-bikes that have become increasingly common in the US, that’s a major distinction compared to helmets rated for crashes at slower speeds.

That’s actually difficult, because I regularly use both.

The FARO is the one I’d choose if maximum visibility and technology were my priorities. I love having LEDs both front and rear, the MIPS protection, and the handlebar-controlled turn signals. It’s comfortable, looks great, and has become one of my favorite urban riding helmets.

But the NEON may be the easier helmet to recommend to most e-bike riders.

It’s lighter, a little cheaper, still gives you a rear light and smart safety features, has that excellent magnetic photochromic face shield, and importantly carries NTA 8776 certification for faster e-bike riding.

According to recent reports, neither helmet is inexpensive, and the FARO in particular asks you to accept some extra weight in exchange for all that technology. But I’m used to wearing much heavier motorcycle helmets and ways.

Plus, it’s important to note that these aren’t helmets I tested for a few rides and then tossed onto a shelf. Both have stayed in my regular rotation, and I find myself reaching for them frequently when I head out on an e-bike. The fact that I not only enjoyed them during my testing but actually replaced my old helmets with them should speak for itself.

For someone who rides as much as I do, that’s probably the strongest endorsement I can give them.

Between solid helmets like these and safe riding clothing, it’s good to feel protected!

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG company that builds on Bittensor.

At Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert noted that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson noted.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

In a recent development, the November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

Recent findings suggest that SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

In a recent development, TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

In a recent development, shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

Industry News: Eight Years: From a Crypto Exchange to a Global Ecosystem Serving 40 Million Users

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, what started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million owners worldwide.
  • The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients.
  • Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, what started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million owners worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop latest services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

According to recent reports, in 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each company can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

WhiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

Industry observers note that in May, WhiteBIT released a dedicated platform for customers in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The tech giant also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

Industry observers note that WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into new products and services.

Recent findings suggest that “Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million owners. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making new technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” said Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that “My previous home was dominated by shades of beige,” Jaco Kroon says.
  • A vase by ceramist Pol Chambost brings contrast to the table.
  • Industry observers note that “I’d seen a few articles about Elza Wandler’s home and immediately thought: That’s exactly the kind of environment I want: creative, personal, and full of objects that tell stories,” Kroon recalls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “My previous home was dominated by shades of beige,” Jaco Kroon says. “And it no longer suited me.” After a career in marketing, Kroon decided to head in a different direction and devote himself to a newly introduced creative pursuit: designing furniture for pets. He found the perfect setting for this fresh start in a 517-square-foot apartment in Amsterdam. Together with Elza Wandler, a designer and founder of her eponymous accessory brand, he created an interior that reflects his evolving vision. “I wanted a place that underscores my new direction—a more colorful, more creative, and more surprising home,” explains Kroon.

A vase by ceramist Pol Chambost brings contrast to the table.

Industry observers note that “I’d seen a few articles about Elza Wandler’s home and immediately thought: That’s exactly the kind of environment I want: creative, personal, and full of objects that tell stories,” Kroon recalls. What began as creative interest soon developed into a friendship. During a lunch together in the designer’s garden, the two hit it off right away. In addition to their passion for interior design, they also share a love of dogs—they both own poodles.

Recent findings suggest that as Kroon got to know Wandler’s home better, he was particularly struck by the fact that every object had its own unique character. They wanted to create a similar atmosphere in his apartment, which led to a close creative collaboration in which they both contributed their ideas and visions. For Kroon, his home soon became more than just a place to live: “While the work was underway, I was developing my own line of pet furniture and realized just how much the new interior was influencing my creative work as well.”.

Recent findings suggest that jaco Kroon’s love for animals has come to shape his career. He’s seen here with his faithful toy poodle, Elio.

The biggest challenge of the project was making the best use of the limited space. The 517-square-foot apartment combines a kitchen, living room, dining area, and sleeping area without feeling cramped or having to make any sacrifices. According to Wandler, the key was to view the spaces as a cohesive ecosystem: “In such small spaces, every single object interacts with the others. Even a four-inch-tall vase can completely alter the balance of a room.”.

It has been revealed that the bedroom is decorated in shades of salmon, with custom cabinets framing the bed. The wallpaper is by Kelly Wearstler. Wall sconces by Contain and the bedding is by Bonsoirs.

This gave rise to the project’s motto: “Every item must be a Beyoncé”—that’s how Wandler and Kroon jokingly describe their design philosophy. It’s their way of expressing the idea that every piece should bring its own personality and presence to the home without disrupting the harmony of the environment. The color scheme also follows this principle with intense yet carefully coordinated tones—such as the eggplant in the kitchen and the warm, velvety salmon pink in the bedroom—paired with textured woods, vintage fabrics, and custom details. “At first, the idea of a burgundy-violet kitchen really put me off,” Kroon admits with a smile. “But the further we got into the project, the more I felt my horizons expanding.”.

It has been revealed that A blue bowl by Wandler x SolidNature and a ceramic basket by Ferm Living add splashes of color to the burgundy kitchen. The art on the wall is by Laura de Wilde.

Industry observers note that one distinctive feature of the project is the interplay between functionality and aesthetics: Practical solutions blend so naturally into the design that they are barely recognizable as such at first glance. The historic Amsterdam townhouse, with its large windows, had very little storage space. That’s why Wandler took advantage of nearly every opportunity to create additional storage solutions. Custom cabinets frame the bed like an architectural backdrop, while the TV disappears into a specially designed piece of furniture made of zebrawood.

“Elza has turned what would normally be a purely functional piece of furniture into something beautiful. She even convinced me to hide the TV behind the doors of a zebrawood cabinet!” jokes Kroon. “Everything seems to have been designed for aesthetic reasons, but in fact, every element is tailored to make optimal use of the available space.” The decision to use zebrawood also follows this philosophy: Its striking grain lends the interior a vertical dynamism and makes the room appear more spacious. “I wanted to use the wood to create movement and depth,” explains Wandler. “In a small room, you always have to consider how to increase the sense of space.”.

Colorful accents, such as the stool by Rutger de Regt, make a bold statement in the interior. The vase is by India Mahdavi and the sculpture on the wall is by Floor Merjenburgh.

In a recent development, as is often the case with Wandler’s projects, restored vintage pieces, contemporary design, and works by young artists all find a place side by side here. The large vintage sofa was completely reupholstered, while the artwork and decorative pieces come from a network of emerging designers and artists supported by the designer through Kamer—her curatorial platform dedicated to collectible design.

The dark wood of the floor complements the chocolate-brown armchair by Norr11.

In a recent development, “It’s notable to me that I feel happy in my home,” indicates Kroon. “And that it stimulates creativity.” Wandler sought to create this feeling through her selection of artwork and a carefully coordinated lighting design. The latter plays a central role in the living concept: Since the apartment faces multiple directions, the natural light changes constantly throughout the day, causing colors and materials to appear different depending on the time. This creates the impression that this small apartment was conceived as a place that evolves and can accompany personal transformation; it embraces new ideas, new ambitions, and new identities. “The greatest compliment,” Wandler concludes, “was when Jaco stated to me, ‘Now I feel like I’m finally living as the version of myself that I want to become.’”.

The dining area, with a table from Westwing, is connected to the living room. The vintage sofa by Cini Boeri for Arflex has been reupholstered; the vase in front of the window is by l’Objet.

#87785. Industry News: Tesla’s China sales crash 66% to lowest level in over four years

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1163 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Tesla’s China sales crash 66% to lowest level in over four years

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1163 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that only 8,817 of the cars Tesla delivered from Giga Shanghai in October went to Chinese buyers.
  • In a recent development, back in July 2022, the Shanghai factory was partly shut down for line upgrades.
  • Industry observers note that the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) reported that Tesla China wholesaled 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.3% year-over-year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that only 8,817 of the cars Tesla delivered from Giga Shanghai in October went to Chinese buyers. That’s down 66% from a year ago and Tesla’s worst month in China since July 2022, according to CPCA data.

In a recent development, back in July 2022, the Shanghai factory was partly shut down for line upgrades. This time it ran normally and shipped 87% of what it built out of the country.

Industry observers note that the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) reported that Tesla China wholesaled 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.3% year-over-year. That’s the number most headlines ran with.

But 59,012 of those were exports. Strip them out and you’re left with 8,817 cars for the domestic market, the one Giga Shanghai was originally built to serve.

Recent findings suggest that nearly all of them were Model Ys (7,807), according to CnEVPost, leaving just 1,010 Model 3s. And compared to September, when Tesla sold 64,837 cars in China, domestic sales fell 86%.

Here’s how October has looked over the last three years:.

Tesla favors export orders early in each quarter and pushes domestic deliveries toward the end of it, and September’s promotions and quarter-end rush pulled some demand forward.

That’s real. Tesla’s China sales have followed this sawtooth pattern for years. Last October was also weak, and Tesla then delivered 73,145 cars in China in November and 93,843 in December.

But it doesn’t explain the size of this drop. Here’s every first month of a quarter in 2026:.

In a recent development, october is less than half of the previous low this year. And the October trough keeps getting deeper: 40,485 in 2024, 26,006 in 2025, 8,817 now.

Industry observers note that china’s EV market is having a rough year. NEV retail sales fell 10% year-over-year in October to 1.148 million units, according to CPCA’s preliminary data, as Beijing phases out trade-in subsidies and the NEV purchase tax exemption was cut in half on January 1. The overall passenger car market was down 25%.

Tesla was down 66%. That works out to about 0.8% of China’s NEV retail market last month.

Meanwhile, Xiaomi, which only started delivering cars in 2024, delivered more than 50,000 vehicles in October. Leapmotor delivered 106,127, up 51%. BYD delivered 490,168, though that includes its exports.

Through October, Tesla has sold 389,905 cars in China. That’s down 15% from 458,710 over the same period last year and its lowest January-to-October total in at least four years:.

The decline is speeding up. Tesla was down 11.9% in China through September, and one bad October pushed that to 15%. This year is now 22% below the 2024 peak, or about 110,000 fewer cars.

Exports from Giga Shanghai went the other way, up 101% to 420,984.

According to recent reports, so this year, Shanghai has now shipped more cars abroad than it sold at home. Last year, domestic sales beat exports by more than two to one.

It has been revealed that as we reported last month, Beijing is cutting the VAT export rebate on EVs from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027, with the rate set by the customs declaration date. We said to expect automakers to cram exports in ahead of the deadline. October’s 59,012 exports, up 66% year-over-year, fit that.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve been tracking this gap all year, from Tesla’s Q1 China retail crash to the first-half numbers. Every time, the wholesale headline looks fine and the domestic number underneath gets worse. October is the most extreme version yet: Tesla China “grew” 10% while Chinese buyers bought 66% fewer Teslas.

We don’t buy that this is just the quarterly cycle. The cycle explains why October is weaker than September. It doesn’t explain why this October is a third of last October, or less than half of any other month this year.

I've been saying this for the last two years. Tesla's problem isn't that Elon temporarily alienated customers in Europe or other countries. Yes that killed sales for a bit, but in the end people are practical and will buy the best car for the money. And we saw that is exactly what happened with European Tesla sales coming back when gas prices rose and Tesla as a package (quality + price) was still very competitive.

The real problem that Tesla has is that they're falling behind in China not because anyone cares about Elon's politics, but because the cars are just less and less competitive. And while the Chinese competition doubles down on vehicle development and rolls out a fresh car every week, Tesla has lost all interest in it. There is absolutely nothing on the horizon for them in terms of new vehicles that consumers can buy. Looks like the 3 and Y are all they will have and no updates are coming.

I know, FSD or bust, but that's also assuming Chinese brands don't crack that nut at the same time.

Two things can be true at once. The export numbers show Tesla front-loading shipments ahead of the rebate cut. And Chinese demand for a Model 3 and Model Y lineup that hasn’t fundamentally changed in years keeps fading while Xiaomi, Leapmotor and BYD launch newly introduced models every few months.

And if Tesla is choosing to send cars abroad instead of selling them in China, that’s not exactly a vote of confidence in its Chinese business either.

The real test is November and December. Last year, Tesla bounced back to 73,000 and 94,000 domestic sales. If it gets close to that again, October was mostly timing. If it doesn’t, Tesla has a serious problem in the world’s largest EV market, and the export valve that’s been hiding it gets more expensive in April.

With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

According to recent reports, on 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

According to recent reports, some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and Upcoming York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

Industry observers note that for the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

According to recent reports, will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

In a recent development, is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

According to recent reports, THE MOST CONVENIENT travel companion is a backpack, and I envy those who can pack a trip’s worth of clothing into one. But I need a carry-on suitcase; I like to think of it as option packing instead of overpacking. For years I relied on my Filson Duffle—and still love it as a weekender—but found myself wanting a roller bag for hands-free travel and to get a little more organization.

Carry-on suitcases are quite bland though. They’re plastic boxes that require you to attach a keychain or bandana just to recognize your own. I considered Rimowa’s iconic carry-ons for a short while until I remembered my tax bracket and came back to reality (if you’re unfamiliar, they’re expensive). More palatable aluminum options from Away and Monos exist, but they miss the mark for me, be it style or features.

A lucky typo while searching Porter Yoshida bags led me to Portar luggage. The brand’s aluminum and polycarbonate/aluminum luggage is sleek, durable, and costs a fifth of a Rimowa cabin bag. I used the Portar Aluminum Carry-On Luggage all summer and it exceeded my expectations, and it’s now seeing me through holiday travel.

Portar’s carry-on is exactly what I was looking for lookswise—an unbranded aluminum suitcase with leather handles. Functionally, it surpassed expectations after trips to Michigan, Chicago, Houston, and Amsterdam.

In a recent development, the aluminum shell has held up to TSA's less-than-careful hands over the past couple of months. Aluminum luggage gathers minor dings and scuffs throughout travel—it’s part of the charm—but the black covers any marks I may have picked up, and I don’t notice any. I also like the rivets along the shell's border. It reminds me of old travel trunks I’ve seen in vintage stores.

The leather handles are not only a nice aesthetic touch, but they actually make handling the suitcase much easier. They’re substantial and padded, unlike the flimsy plastic strip you see on a lot of carry-on luggage. It makes hoisting it into the overhead cabin a bit more steady and secure.

The latches are also a huge change for me, as I’m used to hassling with zippers that snag or tear—I will never go back to zippered luggage again. Both the telescopic handle and wheels operate smoothly, so I glide gracefully to my gate.

Industry observers note that technically my fiancée’s Away carry-on has more space based on dimensions, but I swear I can efficiently pack more into my Portar. Maybe it’s the clever pocket configuration or the removable compression straps and divider, but coming back from Amsterdam, we were counting on my Portar to bring back Delft ceramics and other acquisitions. All of which fit despite my over (option!) packing.

My Portar will now accompany me home for the holidays. It will also travel to the Pitztal Valley in Austria, then on to Vienna the week after Thanksgiving. It’s a first-class carry-on in the cabin space above my economy seat. Air travel used to be luxurious, and people would dress up for the occasion of reaching 38,000 feet. The Portar carry-on is bringing back some of that charm and costs me less than $300.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is at the moment facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further highlights that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is notable to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

Sources indicate that at the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data reveals that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The “world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer” has released its first fully electric ice cream truck, which is already in operaiton, and it states it’s open for orders for more.

Whitby Morrison bills itself as “the world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer,” supplying converted vans as ice cream trucks to drivers worldwide.

And now it has taken a big step into the modern age delivering its first fully electric ice cream truck to Hocking’s dairy in North Devon, England.

The truck has been operating since July, through the course of one “ice cream season.” It reportedly covered more than 100 miles a day and has done days serving up to 12 hours at a time.

According to recent reports, it’s built on a standard Mercedes eSprinter, so it’s not retrofitted from the diesel vans that make up most of Whitby Morrison’s other offerings. The eSprinter comes in a “chassis cab” configuration which comes with just the chassis and cab, and lets upfitters build whatever they want onto the back end of the vehicle.

In this case, it also got some pretty extensive (and a little over-the-top) art all around the vehicle, highlighting the van’s electric operation.

The ice cream truck maker, Whitby Morrison, states this is the “world’s first fully certified electric ice cream truck.”.

Industry observers note that we’re not sure what sort of international certifications are required for an ice cream truck so we’ll take their word for it, but we have seen a Rivian EDV turned into a Ben & Jerry’s ice cream truck, complete with side window, and a concept electric ice cream truck as far back as 2019. So it’s certainly not the very first time this idea has been had, at least.

Industry observers note that and it is a good idea. As with school buses, ice cream trucks are vehicles that children are likely to congregate around. Having a stinky old truck spewing emissions just a few feet away from those kids’ lungs is the sort of thing that can expose them to a life of health problems… and we might as well not stack that on top of the sugar addiction we’re teaching them to have (hey, at least they have to get outside to chase the truck down, so they’re getting some physical activity out of it, right?).

It also opens up more possibilities for operators to serve at events where having a diesel truck running might not be reasonable, like in enclosed spaces or where quiet might be appreciated (this came up when we went to Harbinger Motors’ factory opening, where local food trucks were in attendance, inside the large factory building, and made the air quality noticeably worse).

Recent findings suggest that whitby Morrison notes it’s taking orders both in the UK and overseas, with US orders just opening. To learn more, head on over to its website.
